151.explanation: Preventive Control Tower controls and Organizations SCPs can restrict both Region usage and internet connectivity. Detective Config rules only report violations.

157.explanation: Export database audit logs to CloudWatch Logs and use AWS Backup retention for five-year backups. These are the two options explicitly marked correct in the supplied notes.

158.explanation: CloudFront distributes both live HTTP streams and stored video close to viewers.

159.explanation: WAF filters malicious web requests; IAM authorization restricts API access to authorized identities. API keys identify usage-plan clients and must not be treated as authentication or authorization. This is a reasoned answer based on current AWS guidance.

160.explanation: S3 Standard provides immediate access without the database or search-cluster overhead of the other choices.

178.explanation: AWS Backup centralizes cross-Region copies for supported EC2 and RDS backups.

179.explanation: Attach a role to the EC2 instance with parameter read access and permission to decrypt the parameter encryption key.

184.explanation: Attach Lambda to the VPC so it can use the existing private network path to the on-premises database.

191.explanation: Run reporting reads on a read replica so they do not compete with order processing on the primary database.

192.explanation: Textract extracts text from scans, Comprehend Medical identifies medical entities, and S3 with Athena provides managed storage and SQL analysis.

references.title: Medical document extraction with Textract and Comprehend Medical

193.explanation: Redis caches repeated database reads and supports replicated, highly available deployments. Read replicas distribute reads but do not remove them.

194.explanation: A replicated database cluster across Availability Zones provides failover without waiting to rebuild a single failed server.

195.explanation: Queue orders durably in SQS and let Auto Scaling workers consume them, so processing can resume after an outage.

196.explanation: Set each item expiration timestamp and enable DynamoDB TTL. Expiration cleanup is asynchronous; filter expired items when reading if needed.

197.explanation: Use the Windows .NET Elastic Beanstalk platform and RDS for Oracle Multi-AZ to preserve application and database compatibility.

198.explanation: EKS preserves Kubernetes deployment tooling, Fargate manages worker compute, and DocumentDB offers MongoDB-compatible storage. Check supported MongoDB features during migration.

199.explanation: Transcribe provides speaker-separated transcripts; Athena supports SQL analysis of transcripts stored in S3. Configure seven-year S3 retention separately.

200.explanation: A Cognito user-pool authorizer validates tokens at API Gateway without a custom Lambda authorizer.

207.explanation: SQS buffers requests durably while Lambda controls writes to the provisioned DynamoDB capacity.

210.explanation: Separate queues decouple collection and fulfillment. Backlog per instance gives each worker group a scaling target proportional to pending work.

219.explanation: Use memory-optimized instances for in-memory work and collect application metrics with the CloudWatch agent. Memory is not a default EC2 metric.

224.explanation: Multivalue routing returns healthy addresses with roughly random distribution. Two instances in each of two Availability Zones retain capacity after a zone failure.

232.explanation: Analyze accepted SSH and RDP flows in CloudWatch Logs and notify through metric alarms. Flow logs indicate network connections, not proof of a successful operating-system login.

235.explanation: Schema conversion plus full load and CDC migrates the database and tracks changes. Memory helps buffer a heavy change stream. Bidirectional writes still need a conflict-management plan.

247.explanation: Allow long transactions to finish and enable automated backups before creating an RDS read replica.

257.explanation: Stream CloudWatch metrics through Firehose into S3 without adding work to instance launch scripts.

283.explanation: FSx for NetApp ONTAP supports concurrent NFS and SMB access to shared volumes.

298.explanation: Use separate subnets in both Availability Zones, distribute application instances, and enable RDS Multi-AZ failover.

308.explanation: Inspect the account running the database and its RDS reservation recommendations. Active databases call for reservation optimization rather than idle-instance checks.

311.explanation: SNS subscription filters route each quote type into its own durable SQS queue for independent processing.

315.explanation: Amazon Inspector scans EC2 software for vulnerabilities and generates findings that can drive automated reporting.

327.explanation: Route outbound traffic through Network Firewall and allow only approved repository domains. Security groups cannot filter by URL.

341.explanation: Of these options, the Lake Formation ingestion and Athena path supports centrally enforced column permissions for QuickSight.

366.explanation: With Cognito already providing identity, usage plans and API keys can distinguish subscription API offerings. Keep Cognito authorization in place; an API key alone is not an authorization boundary.

390.explanation: Store sessions outside individual application servers. DynamoDB and replicated Redis are the offered shared session-store options; configure Redis replication and recovery for resilience.

402.explanation: The default Kinesis retention is 24 hours. A consumer running every other day needs a longer retention window.

414.explanation: S3 File Gateway exposes a familiar share and asynchronously uploads new writes to S3 without a custom transfer workflow.

417.explanation: Compute Savings Plans cover both EC2 and Lambda. Connecting Lambda to the application private subnets provides direct access.

423.explanation: IAM identity-based policies attach to users, groups, or roles. Among these options, roles and groups are valid.

429.explanation: The allow statement is limited to us-east-1. The explicit deny blocks StopInstances and TerminateInstances without MFA, overriding the allow. Other Regions have no allow in this policy.

434.explanation: Pre-provision the recovery load balancer and Auto Scaling group, replicate data with global tables, and use DNS failover to reduce recovery work.

477.explanation: DeleteObject is an object-level action and needs the object ARN ending in /*. The existing bucket ARN alone does not grant deletion.

491.explanation: A standard SQS queue supports at-least-once processing. An encrypted-queue consumer needs kms:Decrypt on the KMS key.

528.explanation: Transfer Family keeps FTP ingestion managed. S3 arrival events start Lambda processing, which can delete each object after success.

539.explanation: Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates disk changes with an RPO measured in seconds and recovery typically in minutes.

543.explanation: Use the purchasing account as the Organizations management account and enable discount sharing there for member accounts.

569.explanation: EventBridge publishes matched-event and target-invocation metrics in the AWS/Events namespace.

581.explanation: Two On-Demand instances in each of two Availability Zones leave two running instances after either zone fails.

599.explanation: Customers provide site power, networking, physical access control, and workload spare capacity. AWS maintains the Outposts rack hardware and managed infrastructure.

608.explanation: Associate a WAF web ACL with the ALB and allow the registered addresses using IP sets. Split the list across sets when service quotas require it.

638.explanation: Generate short-lived presigned URLs with a suitably scoped role to grant object access without provisioning employee IAM users.

679.explanation: The supplied notes list B, C, E. A default retention period requires S3 Object Lock; versioning alone does not protect retention. Select Object Lock, a 30-day default retention, and lifecycle expiration. Object Lock enables versioning. For permanent removal of versions, also configure the appropriate noncurrent-version expiration policy.
